summary: Check a JWT somebody else issued: signature, algorithm, exp and nbf. Not how you authenticate your own users.
description: JWT Verify checks a token against the secret on Key and, only if it verifies, puts the payload on Claims. It refuses a token whose header names any algorithm other than the one you selected — which is what stops both `alg: none` and algorithm confusion — and it checks nbf and exp with an optional clock tolerance. Nothing in a token can be believed before the signature check, so Claims is left alone on any failure rather than handed over unchecked. IMPORTANT: this is for OTHER people's tokens — a partner's signed webhook, an OIDC id_token, a link your own backend minted with JWT Sign. Your own callers are already resolved: the Request node outputs Authenticated and User Id from the session token before the graph runs.
whenToUse: A partner hands you a signed token; an identity provider returns an id_token; you are checking back a link you minted with JWT Sign. Never for your own session tokens.

ports.key: The secret the issuer signed with. Wire this from a Secret node.
ports.algorithm: The algorithm the token MUST carry. A token claiming anything else is refused unread.
ports.clockTolerance: Seconds of leeway on exp and nbf, for issuers whose clock is not quite yours. Default 0.
ports.valid: True when the token verified; false whenever Failure fired.
ports.claims: The payload — set only after the signature verified.
ports.failure: Fires when it did not, for any reason. Error says which.
ports.error: Why the token did not verify.

patterns: Request receive → Secret Do → JWT Verify Do, with Failure wired to a Response that answers 401.
Wire both Done and Failure. A function that only wires the happy path hangs when the token is bad.
antiPatterns: Using this to authenticate your own app's users. The Request node's Authenticated and User Id already did that.
Reading Claims off the Failure path. It is deliberately not set there.
